column1: # Dormancy registry for the Prometheus alert rules in this chart.
# A rule that loads is not a rule that can fire. Every rule below references at
# least one series that does not exist on the live Prometheus, so its expression
# cannot become true. Sleeping is not automatically a defect -- a rule watching
# HPA objects that do not exist is correctly asleep -- but the reason has to be
# written down where the reader can find it:
#   object_absent     the object family is not deployed; the rule wakes with it
#   component_absent  the component the rule watches is not deployed -- a defect,
#                     not dormancy: what the rule protects does not exist either
#   feature_off       the feature is not configured (no remote write, ...)
#   collector_off     the exporter is up but this collector is not enabled
#   exporter_version  the source binary's version does not expose the family
#   series_renamed    upstream renamed/removed the series; the rule needs a fix
#   known_defect      a defect that is declared, with the fix named in why
# the private brain repo) treats an absent series without a row here as red.
# A row whose series is back (or whose rule is gone) is reported as stale and
# must be deleted -- the condition it describes is no longer true.
# --- component_absent (9 rules): the delivery chain is not deployed ----------

column4: No Alertmanager is deployed (activeAlertmanagers=[]); this rule is the only witness that alert delivery has no home.
No Alertmanager is deployed; the replica config drift this rule guards cannot occur yet.
No Alertmanager is deployed; there is no notification path to fail. Deploying Alertmanager (or a webhook relay) is the fix.
No Alertmanager is deployed; same delivery gap as AlertmanagerClusterFailedToSendAlerts.
No Alertmanager is deployed; the HA peer set this rule watches does not exist.
No Alertmanager is deployed; cluster membership cannot diverge with zero members.
Prometheus has no Alertmanager target, so the notification counters are never registered; the rule and the defect it reports are the same absence.
Prometheus has no Alertmanager target; partial-send failures cannot be measured before any send exists.
The notification queue has no receiver and therefore no depth; it stays absent until Alertmanager exists.

column1: # --- exporter_version (14 rules): the source version does not expose it -----

column4: kube-state-metrics v2 dropped the kube_*_labels families; kube_job_info carries only allowlisted labels, which are off. The name appears only inside an unless clause, so its absence does not stop the rule from firing: it only makes the label_excluded_from_alerts opt-out inert. Restore by widening the allowlist and rewriting the clause to kube_job_info.

Same removed family as KubeJobNotCompleted, and again only inside an unless clause, so filling-volume alerts still fire; the opt-out is inert until the allowlist carries the label and the clause reads kube_persistentvolumeclaim_info.
Same removed family and same unless-only position as KubePersistentVolumeFillingUp; the inode rule fires, its opt-out does not.

kube_pod_status_reason is exported per reason only while a pod carries one (SchedulingGated et al.); no series means no pod is gated, and the unless clause then excludes nothing while the rule still fires on its phase/ready side.
kubelet_evictions is an ALPHA counter labelled by eviction_signal, created on the first increment; no series means no eviction happened, and the rule fires as soon as one does. Not removed upstream.
The certificate-manager family exists only while kubelet runs with --rotate-certificates; k3s leaves it off, so this is a config gap, not an upstream removal. Enabling rotation would expose it.
Same certificate-manager gate: emitted only with --rotate-certificates enabled.
Same certificate-manager gate: emitted only with server certificate rotation enabled.
Same certificate-manager gate: emitted only with server certificate rotation enabled.

column1: # --- collector_off (5 rules): node-exporter collectors not enabled ----------

column4: The bonding collector is enabled by default in node-exporter and this host runs it -- node_scrape_collector_success{collector="bonding"} reads 0 because the host has no /proc/net/bonding at all, not because the collector is off. No bond device exists, so the family is empty; it is exported as soon as a bond is created and the rule then reads it.

The mdadm collector is enabled by default and reads success=1 on this host; /proc/mdstat lists the personalities but no arrays, so the family is legitimately empty. Create an array and the series appear.
Same collector and same reason as NodeRAIDDegraded: mdadm runs (success=1) and exports per-disk state once an array exists; this host has none.

The systemd collector is the one opt-in collector among the three: node_scrape_collector_success has no series for it at all, and enabling it needs --collector.systemd plus the host dbus socket mounted into the pod. Turning it on can make node-exporter fail to start, so it is a deployment decision, not a flip.
Same opt-in collector as NodeSystemdServiceCrashlooping; absent from node_scrape_collector_success means it was never asked to run.
